newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES SOFTER IN CASH FLUSH MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES SOFTER IN CASH FLUSH MARKET.

text.p: Zimbabwe's short-term trading rates were quoted largely easier in a market flush with cash on Friday, dealers said.

The central Reserve Bank forecast a Z$806 million surplus for Friday and issued 91-day treasury bills worth Z$400 million to discount houses, at 24.99 percent. A second auction for 61-day paper was expected to raise another Z$400 million.
Meanwhile, treasury bills were being traded on the secondary market at 24.75 percent, slightly down from 24.85 percent the previous day, while call money softened to 22.5 from 25.5 percent.

NCD bills redeemable after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought unchanged at 27 percent but sold easier at 25 from 25.6 percent, with bank acceptance bills down to 26 from 26.5 percent (buying) and to 24.85 percent from 25.25 percent on the sell side.
